component.name: NZXT CAM
component.summary: Run NZXT CAM on Linux and drive your NZXT hardware

description.p: NZXT CAM is NZXT's own software for their coolers, fans and RGB controllers. It is Windows-only. This package runs it on Linux under a patched build of Wine, with the sensor plumbing that makes its readings come from Linux itself.

ul.li: The cooler is detected and driven over WinUSB
Pump and fan curves, applied and persisted
Live frames pushed to the cooler's LCD
Liquid temperature, pump and fan RPM
CPU and GPU temperature, clock and load, taken from the kernel's own hwmon and DRM interfaces and usable as curve sources or on the LCD
Per-channel RGB lighting on the cooler and its fans

description.p: NZXT CAM itself is not included. It is downloaded from NZXT the first time the application starts. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by NZXT.

One step needs root on the host and cannot be done from inside the sandbox: installing a udev rule so that NZXT devices are readable by your user. Run "flatpak run --command=nzxt-cam-setup io.github.adds39939.NzxtCamLinux --udev-help" for the exact commands. If you already use liquidctl or OpenRGB, their rules cover it.
Verified with an NZXT Kraken Elite V2. The work is generic rather than model-specific, so other NZXT devices may well work, but none have been tested.

screenshot.caption: The dashboard, with CPU and GPU telemetry read from Linux

description.p: First Flatpak release. Wine, patched, is bundled -- nothing is needed on the host except a udev rule.
